_readMeFirst: v0.16.0 adds the secure browser authentication/bootstrap foundation. D1 remains the target durable source of truth and IndexedDB the browser cache/offline layer. Production browser mode remains intentionally disabled until local-state migration/reconciliation, the real PWA origin, and complete UI read/write routing are in place.

targetArchitecture.status: Dedicated Worker/D1 backend is deployed and verified; v0.14.0 added the guarded browser cache bridge, v0.15.0 added durable user-state routes, and v0.16.0 adds secure browser-session bootstrap while production browser activation and live providers remain pending

pwa.backendCacheBridge: src/lib/backend-cache.ts -> BackendClient.getSnapshot -> repo.applyBackendSnapshot -> atomic IndexedDB replacement
pwa.offlineRule: failed Worker fetch keeps prior IndexedDB cache; backend-hydrated cache is never overwritten by fixture seeding
pwa.initialActivationGuard: backend takeover is allowed only for a genuinely empty cache; fixture/local and legacy non-empty caches require later explicit migration/reset
pwa.legacyCacheRule: v0.13-and-older caches without data_source are detected from actual stored rows and tagged as fixtures on normal startup
pwa.backendCacheMutationMode: local-only user mutations and synthetic provider sync remain blocked while a Worker/D1 snapshot cache is active until active UI writes are routed through BackendClient
pwa.customServiceRenderingRule: user/provider/service-controlled text inserted through innerHTML is HTML-escaped across Settings, Detail, Home, Library, History, Search, Discover and Alerts; custom service brand lookup rejects inherited prototype keys; provider deep links are limited to HTTP/HTTPS; focused browser QA exercises hostile synthetic markup
pwa.cacheBoundary: same-origin unauthenticated app assets only; /api, cross-origin, and Authorization-bearing requests bypass Cache Storage

backendFoundation.canonicalTitleKey: ${media_type}-${tmdb_id}, enforced by D1 CHECK plus UNIQUE(media_type, tmdb_id)
backendFoundation.crosswalkUpsertRule: later partial provider payloads preserve already-known Trakt/IMDb/availability IDs when the incoming field is omitted
backendFoundation.canonicalMutationPrecondition: Library/rating/watched-service/override writes validate their canonical references before durable mutation
backendFoundation.seasonOverrideRule: server selects episodes known and released at action date, requires the season to exist, removes legacy season wildcard, and materializes episode-level overrides in one D1 batch; season zero specials are valid
backendFoundation.customServiceKeyRule: local and Worker paths trim, lowercase, collapse non-alphanumeric runs to hyphens and trim edge hyphens; names/keys are bounded to 80 characters, same-name additions reselect, and different-name normalized-key collisions are rejected
backendFoundation.overrideScopeRule: movie overrides require canonical movies and episode/season overrides require canonical series; HTTP routing rejects obvious scope mismatches before D1 and the repository independently enforces the same invariant
backendFoundation.auth: Operational bearer device token from Worker DEVICE_ACCESS_TOKEN secret plus signed browser-session cookies; fail closed if unconfigured
backendFoundation.browserAuth: user-entered DEVICE_ACCESS_TOKEN may be exchanged only through POST /api/auth/session for a signed 30-day HttpOnly Secure __Host-streamarkr_session cookie; token is never embedded or persisted by frontend code
backendFoundation.browserSessionSigning: HMAC-SHA256 over Streamarkr-specific context, expiry and random UUID nonce using DEVICE_ACCESS_TOKEN as key; secret rotation invalidates existing sessions
backendFoundation.cors: credentialed exact APP_ORIGIN only; APP_ORIGIN intentionally not set until real PWA origin exists
backendFoundation.browserSessionOriginRule: cookie-auth requests require exact configured APP_ORIGIN when Origin is supplied; no-Origin cookie auth is accepted only when request URL origin itself equals APP_ORIGIN
backendFoundation.requestTracing: x-request-id on responses; sanitized structured server errors
backendFoundation.localWranglerConfig: wrangler.local.jsonc; local-only placeholder database ID plus preview ID
backendFoundation.localWranglerValidation: scripts/validate-wrangler-d1.mjs applies migrations with --local and verifies schema_version=1, 8 services, titles table, and d1_migrations table
backendFoundation.remoteWranglerConfig: committed account-neutral wrangler.jsonc plus ignored generated .wrangler/deploy config built from STREAMARKR_D1_DATABASE_ID
backendFoundation.remoteDeployPreflight: scripts/deploy-cloudflare.mjs independently resolves literal D1 name streamarkr and requires authoritative UUID match, then verifies DEVICE_ACCESS_TOKEN before remote mutation
backendFoundation.remoteAutoProvisioning: explicitly disabled for D1 identity inspection, secret inspection, D1 migration and Worker deploy

deploymentPolicy.buildSecret: STREAMARKR_D1_DATABASE_ID stored only in Cloudflare Workers Builds
deploymentPolicy.buildToken: Workers Builds token with Worker deployment permissions plus D1 Edit, scoped to the Streamarkr account
deploymentPolicy.runtimeSecret: DEVICE_ACCESS_TOKEN stored only in Cloudflare Worker Variables & Secrets
deployOrder: resolve named remote D1 streamarkr and require UUID match

hardenedBehaviors: Caught Up requires no gaps through the engaged season while untouched newer seasons are ignored until started
On Hold and Watching Now use real watch timestamps, not manual correction changedAt
Finished series requires provider status Ended
season bulk overrides are bounded to currently known/released episodes and are materialized as episode-level rows so future episodes never inherit an old decision
season bulk overrides require a known season while season zero specials remain valid
availability alerts are transition/cycle-aware
provider-owned availability reconciliation never touches user-owned stores
D1 Library/rating/watched-service/override writes enforce canonical reference and media-scope invariants
local and Worker custom-service paths use the same route-safe normalization and length bounds
same-name custom-service additions reselect while different-name normalized-key collisions are rejected
prototype-like custom service keys cannot resolve inherited object properties in logo branding
user/provider/service-controlled display text is HTML-escaped before innerHTML insertion across all current screens
provider deep links are restricted to HTTP/HTTPS before rendering
D1 provider upserts preserve known optional stable crosswalk IDs across later partial payloads
D1 and IndexedDB availability can retain multiple option types for one title/service
IndexedDB v1->v2 migration recreates/refills only provider-owned availability, preserves user-owned stores, and records invalidation atomically with the versionchange transaction
legacy non-empty local caches cannot be silently replaced by backend state
backend snapshot hydration is atomic and failed refreshes leave prior offline cache untouched
local-only user mutations and synthetic provider sync are blocked while backend cache mode is active
Worker personal routes fail closed without configured auth and unexpected failures do not return raw internal error messages
DEVICE_ACCESS_TOKEN is never embedded or persisted by frontend code; browser bootstrap exchanges a user-entered token for an HttpOnly signed session
browser sessions are integrity-protected, expire after 30 days, fail on tampering, and are invalidated by device-secret rotation
browser-session access and credentialed CORS are exact-origin gated through APP_ORIGIN
service worker never app-shell caches personal API, cross-origin, or Authorization-bearing responses
D1 migration is validated in both Node SQLite and Wrangler local D1 before remote activation
remote config generation never commits the real account identifier
remote deploy verifies named Streamarkr D1 identity and DEVICE_ACCESS_TOKEN before mutation
remote Wrangler automatic provisioning is disabled
normal main merges cannot be the production deployment trigger

absoluteRules: No live provider calls from synthetic QA
No production deploy without fresh explicit authorization
No real/personal data in fixtures or automated QA
Never overwrite user-owned data from provider refresh
Never overwrite existing or legacy local user-owned state during first backend cache activation without an explicit migration/reset step
Never overwrite a valid backend-hydrated offline cache with demo fixtures
Never allow local-only user writes while a Worker/D1 snapshot cache is active
Never cache personal API responses in the app-shell service-worker cache
Never embed or persist DEVICE_ACCESS_TOKEN in public frontend source, generated assets, browser storage, or cookies
Never make browser session cookies script-readable or remove exact-origin validation to work around browser cookie restrictions
Never commit API keys, OAuth secrets/tokens, Cloudflare credentials, real D1 UUIDs, personal data, or BANDMARKR data
Never reuse or modify BANDMARKR Cloudflare resources for Streamarkr
